# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura KS-930 round 3 (#876, tier 1) — GO with two Majors, 2026-09-07 10:29Z** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The best gate this fleet has produced, and the reason is that it corrected the COORDINATOR'S AUTHORISING CRITERION, not just the code.** **(1) It refuted the test Wednesday had ratified on.** Wednesday told the builder *"the base column is the argument"* — base rc1 → head rc0. The tester measured assertion A's first arm at base and found it **UNCONDITIONAL**: every row reads rc1 at base, including all four false-positive controls AND a plant-point control (`RUN apk add --no-cache curl`) naming nothing node-ish. **So the criterion is satisfied by the entire F6 feature Kam ruled in — reused, it would authorise everything.** It then said the ratification still HOLDS on the substantive reading and that it was *"flagging the criterion, not the ruling"* — **the retraction scoped to exactly what its measurement refuted** ([[2026-09-06_a-retraction-inherits-the-scope-of-its-measurement]] from the other side). Criterion retired by Wednesday the same action. **(2) Its largest finding is in NOT-TESTED, where the rules put it and where a weaker pass would have buried it:** every cell ran on macOS BWK awk; **neither gawk nor mawk is on the machine, and CI uses one of those**; the round-3 edit is an alternation whose leftmost-longest behaviour is exactly where implementations differ. **That single paragraph is why Wednesday held the merge.** **(3) It answered the one question only it could** — the `node-exporter` false block is acceptable, on measured grounds (the arm is unreachable across 25 of 25 class files; the token appears nowhere outside the PR's own fixture; leg 13's verdict on the repo's own tree is byte-identical at all three SHAs) — **and then undercut the builder's own justification for it** (F-QA-2: the message the human sees names neither the rule nor a remedy, and a base already in `NON_JS_BASES` still blocks, so the only exit is `--no-verify`, which disables all 13 legs). **(4) Five self-corrections in the open, including two predictions of its own that were WRONG and one malformed inverse-edit that left the guard tampered — caught by its own sha256 restore assertion, which refused to report success.** Its note: *"a driver that had only checked 'did it run' would have carried a tampered guard into every later cell."* **(5) It refused a boundary rather than working around it:** `ls-remote` returned `Permission denied (publickey)` — the Testing Agent project holds no Secuura identity — so it verified the SHA from **three independent local reads plus a branch reflog proving no push landed during the pass**, and filed the remote read under NOT-TESTED. **It also corrected the brief's own phrasing**: leg 13 blocks every push that TOUCHES `Blockchain/Dev`, not literally every push. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s144) | **#884 KS-858/F5 — the `//` rate-limiter bypass: found, fixed, tier-1 GATED to GO, and MERGED to develop at `db94e9fc8`** (2026-09-07, the first merge of the day) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Kam's own words on the chain, panel 09:50: *"Fantastic and genuinely great find."*** Scored 1.0 for a chain in which **every link refused to round anything up.** **(1) It REFUSED a fix-shape Wednesday relayed** — and the gate then re-derived that the refusal was correct: the relayed shape would have repaired the 404 and PRESERVED the bypass. **This is the behaviour to protect above all others in this row.** **(2) It re-measured its OWN defect at wrap** so Kam would rule on the true size, turning

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
